title: Trace exporter dispatcher with tenant-priority queueing and TTL buffering
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: implement a resilient dispatcher for trace export that prioritizes tenant-critical traffic, applies TTL-based buffering for backends under load, and normalizes payload envelopes for downstream Jaeger/Tempo collectors. Background: we've observed tail-latency spikes and backend overload during regional incidents. Current single-path exporter either blocks ingestion or drops spans indiscriminately. This ticket proposes a dispatcher component that sits between OTLP ingestion and exporter plugins, providing: (1) per-tenant priority queues with configurable weights; (2) short-lived TTL buffers for temporarily offline backends with eviction and retry strategies; (3) an envelope normalizer to ensure required fields (traceid, spanid, timestamp) before sending to legacy Jaeger collector endpoints; (4) a graceful degrade path that routes low-priority tenants to a compressed/aggregated export format when capacity constrained. Compatibility: supports OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP clients; exporter plugins for Tempo (HTTP v2) and Jaeger (thrift over HTTP/grpc) will be updated to accept normalized envelopes. Out-of-scope: long-term archival and analytics storage optimization. Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/TE-246/dispatcher-design
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher accepts OTLP traffic and applies tenant priority weights according to config
When a configured backend is unreachable, traces for that backend are buffered for up to TTL (configurable) and then retried with exponential backoff
Low-priority tenants are marked and fall back to aggregated export format (span count + sampled traces) when system-level utilization > 85%
End-to-end integration tests cover Tempo and Jaeger exporters with simulated backend failures
Telemetry: metrics emitted for queue depth per-tenant, buffer eviction rate, dispatch latency P95/P99, and fallback events
Documentation for runtime config and migration notes published in Console docs and runbooks
implementation_notes: Component lives in trace-ingest module as 'dispatcher' with a thin interface: Enqueue(tenant, envelope) and Flush(ctx)
Use a lock-free priority queue per shard keyed by tenant-id to avoid global contention
Buffer backend: in-memory ring buffer with optional short-term disk spill to /var/lib/redwood/trace-buffer for OOM protection
TTL default: 30s with max retries 5; make both configurable per-exporter
Envelope normalizer will coerce legacy jaeger tags to otel.attribute-style keys and drop non-utf8 keys with a warning metric
Add schema-negotiation headers for Tempo HTTP v2 and fallback header mapping for older Jaeger receivers
SLO targets: P95 dispatch latency < 50ms under normal load; P99 < 250ms for high-priority tenants
Plan migration: enable dispatcher behind feature-flag and route 10% of traffic for 48h before global rollout
